How readily a thirsty plant catches pests or blight. 0 means never.
Trees and bushes need watering and can catch pests or blight; a young plant left dry for three days dies. Turn off for a plant-and-forget orchard.
Hover a planted tree or bush to read its growth stage, time to the next stage, fruit, water, condition, and what is in the bucket if it is tapped.
Farming skill needed to plant a seed. Saplings need this plus two, and peaches, blueberries and grapes need one more again.
Scales how much fruit a tree sets. A tree in poor condition still bears less than this.

How fast plants move between growth stages. 2.0 is twice as fast, 0.5 takes twice as long. At 1.0 a fruit tree grown from seed is bearing after about 34 days and full size after about 55; a bush takes about 27. Growth slows or stops in a species' own bad months.
Litres a tapped tree yields per in-game day, before the species multiplier and the season. Red maple runs hardest, the two conifers give under half as much resin. Set to 0 to switch tapping off.

Turn on before removing Orchard, or characters with an Orchard job or trait will not load. Load and save each character once: Orchard traits are taken off and Orchard jobs become Unemployed (skills and items stay). Then remove the mod. On a server, every player must log in once.
Tiles cleared around the square you rake. 0 clears only that tile, 1 clears a three by three.

Hard cap on how many planted trees, bushes, holes and tapped trees the save will track, so a long server run cannot grow the save file forever. Past the cap, planting is refused rather than silently dropped.

On, a seed only goes in during its own sowing months, and planting in the late risk month starts the tree in poor condition. Off, plant anything any month. Also honours the vanilla Plant Growing Seasons setting.
Percent chance that cutting a fruit open yields usable seeds. At 60 you lose roughly two fruit in five.
How many times a tap can be emptied before it splits. A tap you pull out early keeps the collections it has left, so moving one costs you nothing and re-placing it does not renew it.
How many trees one player may have tapped at once. Eight is a round you can walk; raising it mostly means carrying more buckets.

Sap runs on freeze and thaw: hard in February and March, thin either side of them, and not at all through the summer. Pine resin is the other way about and runs fastest in the heat. Turn this off and every tree yields all year.
How fast soil dries between rain. 0 means plants never go thirsty.
How much a plant grows during its own bad months. 0 holds it dormant until the season turns.
Boil it down in a metal bucket over heat. Twice the binder per litre of straining. A wooden bucket will not take the heat.
Boil sap down in a metal bucket over heat until it thickens. Six litres of sap is one bottle of syrup, which is roughly the trade a real sugarhouse makes.
Let the mulch rot down properly into a bag of compost.
A spout and a hook, whittled from a plank. Goes into a tree and stays there.
Dandelion roots and stems weep a white latex. Boil a good armful down and it comes together as crude rubber - which is exactly what was done the last time the world ran out.
The oldest made colour there is - copper, sand and lime fired together into a blue frit. The only blue here that will not fade in the sun.
Cut the fruit open and pick out the pips. Most will not be viable.
Iron steeped with oak tannin and vinegar. Strong for black, thinned for grey.
Shred and turn the leaves until they start to break down.
Cook pine resin down in a metal bucket over heat to a black, sticky tar. Waterproofs, seals, sticks, and burns.
Pitch glue: pine tar cut with charcoal until it sets hard. Nobody is making glue any more, so this is where yours comes from now.
Roll a lump around a twine core and cure it into a length of hose.
Press two lumps into a slab the size of a cut of tire. Anything that wanted tire rubber will take it.
Finely ground pigment. Stir it into paint binder in an empty paint bucket to make a can of paint.
The colour in these berries answers to what you add. Vinegar turns it pink, baking soda turns it blue, and plain water leaves it purple.
Fire copper, sand and lime together until they fuse into a blue frit, then grind it.
Grind the dried material into a fine pigment powder.
Steep iron with oak tannin and vinegar until it blackens.
Blend two cans of paint into a third colour. Ten doses go in and ten come out.
Stir pigment into paint binder in an empty bucket to make a can of paint.
Stir pigment into paint binder in an empty bucket to make a can of paint.
Cut a pigment with white powder to lighten it.
Leave copper standing in vinegar until the blue-green crust forms, then scrape it off.
Settle copper onto powdered chalk for a paler blue-green than verdigris gives.
Strain it through cloth, cold, in any bucket. Simple, and it wastes half of it.
Drive the last of the water off and the syrup grains into sugar. Keeps forever, unlike the syrup.
The blue-green crust that grows on copper left in vinegar. Makes green paint, or cyan if you use less of it.
A paler blue-green, made by settling copper onto chalk. Makes turquoise, or blue at strength.
